definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese poetic form consisting of five lines with a 5-7-5-7-7 mora pattern. One of the oldest forms of Japanese poetry, dating back over a thousand years. Still actively composed today, with newspaper columns and poetry contests keeping the tradition alive.

examples.japanese: {短歌|たんか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧。
⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{短歌|たんか}⟦{欄|らん}→欄：03901_ran⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{毎週|まいしゅう}→毎週：00730_maishuu⟧⟦{投稿|とうこう}している→投稿する：18994_toukousuru⟧。
examples.english: I submit to the newspaper's tanka column every week.

examples.japanese: ⟦{万葉集|まんようしゅう}→万葉集：08827_manyoushuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧4500{首|しゅ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{短歌|たんか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{収|おさ}められている→収める：02022_osameru⟧。
examples.english: The Man'yoshu contains approximately 4,500 tanka poems.

notes:
USAGE: {短歌|たんか} follows a 5-7-5-7-7 mora pattern across five lines. Poems are counted with the counter {首|しゅ}. The verb for composing tanka is ⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧.

The form predates haiku; historically the upper portion (5-7-5) and lower portion (7-7) were sometimes composed by different people as a literary game. In modern times, tanka enjoys renewed popularity especially among younger poets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {短歌|たんか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧: to compose a tanka
- {短歌|たんか}{集|しゅう}: a collection of tanka
- {短歌|たんか}⟦{欄|らん}→欄：03901_ran⟧: tanka column (in a newspaper)
- {一首|いっしゅ}: one tanka poem

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {短歌|たんか}: 31-mora poem (5-7-5-7-7)
- ⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧: 17-mora poem (5-7-5)
- ⟦{和歌|わか}→和歌：05230_waka⟧: Japanese poem (classical umbrella term that includes tanka)
- ⟦{川柳|せんりゅう}→川柳：09660_senryuu⟧: humorous 17-mora poem (5-7-5, no seasonal word required)
